verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 is landed on both limbs the dispatch names. Identity is consistent and unique — artifact platform-tcb-leftover-join.v5 with version 5 — and I read the artifact and version fields of the whole chain to confirm the v2/v3 collision does not recur: v1/1, v2/2, v3/2, v4/4, v5/5. The false sentence is gone, occurring zero times against two in v3, and the two stale predecessor roles are rewritten to the version-agnostic 'Not this artifact's version number', which removes the failure mode rather than re-pointing it at a pair that could go stale again; the single remaining non-reuse sentence correctly names the v5-to-v3 pair. The repair disturbed no measurement: all eight obligations are == identical to v4's, and only the identity and provenance fields differ. The substance holds independently — the named list is == equal to live G22 v1 and live catalog v1, OBL-G22-NAMED-CATALOG is leftoverDesign false, both protected obligations remain leftoverDesign true, OBL-ADVISORY-HONESTY survives byte-identical with all four D-125 advisories and its summary bucket, no TCB table is populated, nothing is SATISFIED, no DR-G* row is added, required-now is 26, all thirty-five cited path/digest pairs measure equal with zero mismatches, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head and live HEAD, and the subject and all four predecessors did not move. The candour is worth recording: predecessorV3 names its own lineage's REJECT, and predecessorV4 admits that v4 set the version but retained the stale sentences and was never independently reviewed — which I confirmed by finding no v4 review file and no review sub-object on that entry alone.
